gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoi: Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined reads modern and spacious, its curves stopping well short of the stems. Vast Shadow is the loud one, cut from a single stroke width in a vintage display voice, while this sans just keeps going.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-h: Modern in feel, Vast Shadow draws every stroke at one width, horizontals no thinner than verticals. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs follows with a tall x-height and outward-pointing tips, so a long passage stays steady and plain.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Vast Shadow looks like twine pressed into a flat surface, vintage and eye-catching with its tall mean line and generous side spacing. Noto Sans Bamum is its calm counterweight.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Monoline from stem to serif, Vast Shadow has a vintage, eye-catching look that no other part of the pair copies. Noto Sans Bassa Vah then brings a huge midsection and a pliers-like open c, which makes the pair feel deliberately mismatched.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Eye-catching, this pair starts with Vast Shadow, bent tubing of one gauge. Noto Sans Buhid then takes over with a high x-height and generous gaps where curves meet stems, so the heading shouts and the text keeps talking quietly.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-cham: Noto Sans Cham is modern and clean, with tall rounded lowercase. Vast Shadow gives the page a pipe-cleaner vintage flourish up top, then that plain sans carries the reading below it.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Vast Shadow has a vintage, eye-catching look, every stroke end as wide as the middle. Noto Sans Cherokee is a friendly plain sans with a tall band of letters, so give the heading extra size and the body less.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-chorasmian: Vast Shadow traces every stroke at the width of a single stylus, giving a vintage, eye-catching face. Its strongest quality is the contrast with Noto Sans Chorasmian, a plain sans with a large x-height and curves that stop short.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic reads clean and modern, with open apertures throughout and ascenders that barely rise above the x-height. Over many paragraphs it stays light and unfussy.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Vintage, bold and hard to miss. Vast Shadow does its best work as a loud display face with constant thickness around curves, while Noto Sans Ethiopic is the sturdy sans, tall in the lowercase and made for steady reading.
